title: Proportional-odds regression for an ordered outcome
summary: One odds ratio for the shift toward higher categories of an ordered outcome, with the cut-point thresholds.

sizing._why: Whitehead's formula for an ordinal outcome needs the anticipated distribution across categories and is not in the catalog; a binary-split form would size a different quantity.

pinned_defaults: Both: the category ORDER is written out. The fixture's words sort alphabetically as mild, moderate, none, severe, and both factor() and pandas would fit that ordering silently.

Both: positive coefficient = higher categories (polr: logit P(Y <= k) = zeta_k - eta; OrderedModel the same). Other software (SAS PROC LOGISTIC by default) models the lower categories and inverts the odds ratio.
Both: tight convergence (polr reltol 1e-14; Newton with tol 1e-12). At defaults statsmodels' BFGS did not converge and the two differed by up to 6e-5.
_proportional_odds: The single odds ratio assumes the same effect at every cut point. Check it (fit the binary splits separately, or a partial proportional-odds model) and state it.
